text:
lina: FYI — got paged this morning: autoscaler removed 2 nodes in us-west1-b and two inference pods were evicted, causing a ~5m tail latency spike. We have PDBs configured but still saw evictions. Anyone seen this pattern before?

raj: Are the inference pods behind a Deployment/ReplicaSet or StatefulSet? CA normally checks PDBs but will skip if it can't reschedule pods elsewhere. Any node labels (preemptible/spot) in play?

michael: They were Deployments (3 replicas each). This one is in our spot GPU nodepool (preemptible) and the cluster had a transient shortage — CA decided to scale down that nodepool and moved pods. PDBs can block voluntary evictions, but if the remaining capacity can't place pods CA considers other nodepools or will force reschedule if it thinks pods are evictible.

abby: Quick tactics that helped us: 1) give inference pods a high PriorityClass so kube-scheduler won't preempt them accidentally and so controllers prefer keeping them; 2) set PDBs with minAvailable (not maxUnavailable) to express exact survivors; 3) mark batch/worker pods as safe-to-evict so CA can pick them first.

jorge: Example snippets we pushed this morning: 

1) PriorityClass:
```yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: inference-critical
value: 1000000
globalDefault: false
description: "High priority for serving inference; reduce risk of scale-down evictions"
```

2) PDB (minAvailable):
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: inference-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference
```

3) Pod annotations to bias autoscaler:
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"    # keep this pod around during scale-down
    controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost: "100"        # higher cost = prefer keeping on node
```

lina: Nice. So if we set safe-to-evict=false on all inference pods, will CA never touch those nodes?

raj: CA respects the annotation, but caveats: if every pod on a node is marked safe-to-evict=false, CA may be unable to drain that node and skip it (good), but if capacity is tight elsewhere CA might pick a different node to remove or you get fragmentation. Also remember PDBs block voluntary eviction only — node failures/force deletes still terminate pods.

michael: Operational tweaks we applied: 
- increase cluster-autoscaler --scale-down-unneeded-time to 10m (gives short flaps time to settle)
- scaleDownUtilizationThreshold -> 0.5 (less aggressive)
- ensure spot/preemptible nodepools have smaller minSize and we prefer removing them via CA expander: least-waste

abby: Another safe pattern: create two nodepools for GPUs — reserved (dedicated capacity) for critical inference with taints + tolerations and higher price, and spot pool for training/batch. Put inference pods on reserved pool via nodeSelector/affinity or by tolerating a taint. Then autoscaler can still aggressively scale the spot pool without touching critical pods.

jorge: If you need a quick mitigation for tonight: 
- patch the PDB to minAvailable=1 (if safe) so CA can't remove too many replicas, or temporarily cordon the reserved nodes: 
```bash
kubectl cordon <node-name>
kubectl annotate node <node-name> cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true
```
- scale up reserved pool by 1 if traffic surge is expected.

oncall-bot: Auto-run: patched inference-pdb -> minAvailable=2 and set safe-to-evict=false on pods in ns=prod-inference. Scaled reserved-gpu-pool +1. Monitoring for 30m.

lina: Thanks — can someone open a short runbook for: (a) two-pool pattern (reserved vs spot) + affinity examples, (b) how/when to use PDB vs priorityclass vs safe-to-evict, and (c) autoscaler knobs we tuned? Want ops playbook we can hand to oncall.

abby: I'll draft a runbook and drop in #eng-docs. Will include sample manifests and the exact CA flags we changed.

raj: Also adding a test: a chaos job that simulates nodepool scale-down in staging to validate nothing critical is evicted.

lina: Perfect. Marking this resolved for now, will watch the monitoring deck. Thanks all :thumbsup:
